arxiv-2203-09869.title: Electromagnetically induced transparency in inhomogeneously broadened divacancy defect ensembles in SiC
arxiv-2203-09869.creator: Olger V. Zwier*, Tom Bosma*, Carmem M. Gilardoni, Xu Yang, Alexander R. Onur, Takeshi Ohshima, Nguyen T. Son, Caspar H. van der Wal
arxiv-2203-09869.description: Abstract Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) is a phenomenon that can provide strong and robust interfacing between optical signals and quantum coherence of electronic spins. In its archetypical form, mainly explored with atomic media, it uses a (near-)homogeneous ensemble of three-level systems, in which two low-energy spin-1/2 levels are coupled to a common optically excited state.

arxiv-2307-03035.title: Tidal debris from Omega Centauri discovered with unsupervised machine learning 2023 Tidal debris from Omega Centauri discovered with unsupervised machine learning – 2
arxiv-2307-03035.creator: Kris Youakim, Karin Lind, Iryna Kushniruk
arxiv-2307-03035.description: Abstract The gravitational interactions between the Milky Way and in-falling satellites offer a wealth of information about the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. In this paper, we explore the high-dimensionality of the GALAH DR3 plus Gaia eDR3 data set to identify new tidally stripped candidate stars of the nearby star cluster Omega Centauri ( ω ​ Cen \omega\,\mathrm{Cen} ).

arxiv-2310-07611.title: Democratizing LLMs: An Exploration of Cost-Performance Trade-offs in Self-Refined Open-Source Models
arxiv-2310-07611.creator: Sumuk Shashidhar, Abhinav Chinta, Vaibhav Sahai, Zhenhailong Wang, Heng Ji
arxiv-2310-07611.description: Abstract The dominance of proprietary LLMs has led to restricted access and raised information privacy concerns. High-performing open-source alternatives are crucial for information-sensitive and high-volume applications but often lag behind in performance. To address this gap, we propose (1) A untargeted variant of iterative self-critique and self-refinement devoid of external influence.

arxiv-2403-02435.title: Gauging Centrifugal Instabilities in Compressible Free-Shear Layers Via Nonlinear Boundary Region Equations
arxiv-2403-02435.creator: Omar Es-Sahli, Adrian Sescu, Yuji Hattori
arxiv-2403-02435.description: Abstract Curved free shear layers emerge in many engineering problems involving complex flow geometries, such as the flow over a backward facing step, flows with wall injection in a boundary layer, the flow inside side-dump combustors, or wakes generated by vertical axis wind turbines, among others.

arxiv-2411-13542.title: The Rényi Outlier Test
arxiv-2411-13542.creator: Ryan Christ, Ira Hall, David Steinsaltz
arxiv-2411-13542.description: Abstract . Cox and Kartsonaki proposed a simple outlier test for a vector of p-values based on the Rényi transformation that is fast for large p p and numerically stable for very small p-values – key properties for large data analysis. We propose and implement a generalization of this procedure we call the Rényi Outlier Test (ROT).

arxiv-2511-06624.title: No-signalling-projection-invariant Bell inequalities
arxiv-2511-06624.creator: Soumyadip Patra, Jitendra Prakash, Aaditya Paudel, Peter Bierhorst
arxiv-2511-06624.description: Abstract In this paper, we highlight how any Bell inequality for a configuration involving n n parties each performing one of m m binary-outcome measurements has a canonical form that is no-signalling-projection invariant. Specifically, the L 2 L^{2} -projection of weakly signalling data onto the no-signalling polytope leaves the violation of this canonical Bell inequality unchanged.

arxiv-2602-04247.title: DementiaBank-Emotion: A Multi-Rater Emotion Annotation Corpus for Alzheimer’s Disease Speech (Version 1.0)
arxiv-2602-04247.creator: Cheonkam Jeong, Jessica Liao, Audrey Lu, Yutong Song, Christopher Rashidian, Donna Krogh, Erik Krogh, Mahkameh Rasouli, Jung-Ah Lee, Nikil Dutt, Lisa Gibbs, David Sultzer, Julie Rousseau, Jocelyn Ludlow, Margaret Galvez, Alexander Nuth, Chet Khay, Sabine Brunswicker, Adeline Nyamathi
arxiv-2602-04247.description: Abstract We present DementiaBank-Emotion, the first multi-rater emotion annotation corpus for Alzheimer’s disease (AD) speech. Annotating 1,492 utterances from 108 speakers for Ekman’s six basic emotions and neutral , we find that AD patients express significantly more non-neutral emotions (16.9%) than healthy controls (5.7%; p p < .001).

pmc-11442705.description: Natural killer (NK) cells play a crucial role in immunotherapy for cancer due to their natural ability to target and destroy cancer cells. pmc-11510792.description: This study examined the effects of late sowing, water restrictions, and interannual weather variations on wheat grain yield and quality through field trials in Spain over two growing seasons. pmc-13167811.creator: Lucy Zhao, Melissa Sweeney, Lewis Carpenter, Savia de Souza, Emma Caton, James Galloway, Andrew Cope, Kirsty Bannister, Elena Nikiphorou, Rona Moss-Morris, Sam Norton
pmc-13167811.description: BackgroundPain is a debilitating and persistent symptom of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), associated with impaired functional capacity and reduced quality of life. pmc-13385530.description: Text-to-motion generation aims to synthesize semantically consistent and naturally coherent motion sequences from natural language descriptions. pmc-13575126.title: In silico insights into the adsorption and detection of dimethyltryptamine on metal doped C20 fullerene
pmc-13575126.creator: Abdulrahman Sumayli, Saad M. Alshahrani, Jawaher Abdullah Alamoudi
pmc-13575126.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Given the psychoactive effects of dimethyltryptamine (DMT), classified as a Schedule I drug, developing diagnostic methods is essential. In this computational study, we investigate the adsorption and sensing behavior of DMT on pristine C20 fullerene and its beryllium (Be), magnesium (Mg), and calcium (Ca) doped derivatives using density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT (TD-DFT), and quantum theory of atoms in molecules (QTAIM) to provide suitable candidates that reduce trial-and-error in subsequent experimental work.
